Part 1 · Setup

Each computer is set up once.

Your PAT stays on your computer. The shared setup — streams, roles, Feature setup — comes from Git for everyone.

Setup · Start here

Home

Opens when the app starts

  1. Setup · n/4 in the top bar shows what is left to set up on this computer
  2. Search pages, streams and settings from Where to?
  3. The menu on the left groups the pages: My Work, Release Details, Admin

Setup · Step by step

Get started

Top bar → Setup · n/4

  1. Click Setup to open the guide
  2. Work through the steps in order; done ones are ticked
  3. Each step opens the right setting for you

The count is per computer: a new laptop starts again at 0/4.

Setup · Step 1

Your work email

My settings → Your work email

  1. Enter your work email, as Azure DevOps knows you
  2. Save

The app uses it to find your work items, hours and PI reviews. A typo shows you nothing.

Setup · Step 2

Servers and PATs

My settings → Servers and PATs

  1. Create a PAT in Azure DevOps: Work Items (Read & Write)
  2. Paste it on the server’s row and Save PAT
  3. On-prem servers need Read only

One PAT per server, saved in this browser only — never in Git.

Setup · Step 3

Git storage

Admin → Data & sharing → Git storage

  1. Enter the repository, branch and data file you were given
  2. Paste your GitHub token (fine-grained, this repository only)
  3. Load: the shared setup arrives for everyone the same

Loading runs in the background — watch it in Jobs done.

Setup · Tool Owner

Stream mapping

Admin → Streams

  1. Each stream: its server, project and query
  2. Set up a stream, then Fetch
  3. Save to Git: everyone gets it at their next start

Only the Tool Owner changes it. Everyone else sees it read-only.

Setup · Admin

People & roles

Admin → People & roles

  1. Names and emails come from Azure DevOps — nothing is typed
  2. Give each person their access roles
  3. Mark as left, or Not part of the team, from the person’s drawer

New person missing? Add them to the team in Azure DevOps, then refresh.

Setup · Admin

Epic & Feature setup

Admin → Epic & Feature setup

  1. Pick an Epic in Setup per Epic
  2. Set its title fields, Definition of Done and User Stories
  3. New Feature under that Epic uses them automatically

This is why every Feature gets the same structure.

Part 2 · Day to day

A normal week in the app.

Book your hours, keep your board current, create Features the same way every time, and review the PI.

Day to day · Every week

Time Writing

My Work → Time Writing

  1. Cards: capacity, planned and actual hours
  2. Your month Tasks: enter planned and actual hours
  3. ＋ Add a new activity for work not in the list, then Save

Mind the last day to update, shown at the top.

Day to day · During the week

My Tasks [Board]

My Work → My Tasks [Board]

  1. Your Features and User Stories in one place
  2. Move them New → Active → Closed
  3. Close on a Feature closes your open children too, after one check

The badge on the menu counts what is waiting for you.

Day to day · When work arrives

New Feature

＋ New Feature on the board, Backlogs or Release Details

  1. Parent Epic first: it decides title, DoD and stories
  2. Start and Target date; month Tasks follow them (tick box)
  3. Pick the User Stories, then Save

Your own User Story is folded away — open it only if you need one.

Day to day · Before the sprint ends

Sprint check

My Work → Sprint check

  1. Finds your items not in the current PI and Sprint
  2. Moves them there in one go
  3. Flags state problems to fix

“Nothing to fix” is the goal.

Day to day · At PI end

My PI Review

My Work → My PI Review

  1. Your Features of the chosen PI and whether each is reviewed
  2. Review… on one row, or Edit review… if you already wrote one
  3. Tick several, then Update review for N…

A greyed tick box tells you why on hover.

Day to day · At PI end

One review, many Features

The review pop-up

  1. Check the list: new comment, or replaces your review
  2. Learnings, Struggles, Move to next PI, Review meeting
  3. Read the Preview, then Post

It is posted to each Feature’s Discussion in Azure DevOps.

Day to day · Background work

Jobs done

Top bar → Jobs done

  1. Long work runs here: loads, bulk posts, fetches
  2. Running, Done, or Needs a look with the reason
  3. Keep working while it runs

A pop-up that closed by itself? Its work is in Jobs done.

Day to day · Reading

Release Details

Release Details → a stream, e.g. DP

  1. The releases of the stream from its query
  2. Each release with its QE and milestone dates
  3. Create Feature on a row, or Create Features for many

Day to day · Reading

Team overview

Data Insights → Team overview

  1. Filter by Year, Quarter, Month, Region, Role, person, stream
  2. Six tiles, each opening its analysis
  3. Reset filters goes back to the current period

Day to day · Reading

My dashboard

Data Insights → My dashboard

  1. Your hours per month, your open work, your streams
  2. Customize to hide or move its sections
  3. Pin pages to the menu

Day to day · Staying current

Force Update

Bottom right of every page

  1. Shows the version you run and the newest one
  2. Loads the newest version
  3. Your data stays: this browser and Git

A page says “A newer version was published”? Press Load the new version.

Day to day · When something new arrives

New app version, or new setup in Git

New version of the app

Press Load the new version — or Force Update at the bottom right. Your data stays.

New shared setup in Git

Press Load everything from Git. It runs in Jobs done; keep working meanwhile.

Good to know

Four rules the app keeps for you

Your PAT stays local

Only in this browser or the desktop app. Never in Git, backups or SharePoint. One PAT per server.

Writes go to dev.azure.com only

On-premises servers are read-only, in the web app and the desktop app.

Long work runs in the background

Loads and bulk posts show in Jobs done; you keep working meanwhile.

New version? Force Update

Bottom right of every page. If a page says a newer version was published, load it.

Part 3 · Your turn

Hands-on checklist

  1. Set your work email
  2. Add your Azure DevOps PAT for the server
  3. Connect Git storage and load
  4. Open Time Writing: check this month’s Tasks
  1. Move one item on My Tasks [Board]
  2. Open New Feature (Cancel before Save)
  3. Run Sprint check on your work
  4. Open My PI Review for this PI

Stuck? Raise a hand — and tell us what the screen says, word for word.
